decision: Leave runtime device flags and completion APIs unchanged. This one-stream probe does not support a wait-policy product experiment as the next high-impact route. Return to structural attention work, retaining the qualified original q8192 boundary.
limitations: Host intervals include kernel submission, event submission and completion observation; they do not isolate API wait cost or use GPU-event elapsed time.
Only the final iteration of each case has five independent CPU output samples and the full redzone comparison. Intermediate iterations are synchronized but not copied.

Four sequential processes with a fixed method order are not a randomized product study. The first process includes larger startup/cold costs; its guarded process wall is not compared as steady-state throughput.
One default stream without a model does not establish all-stream synchronization equivalence. No hipStreamQuery substitution, runtime flag change or inference claim follows.
